title: Honor Launches Record 11,000mAh Phone, Eyes 12,000mAh Next
excerpt: The Honor X80 Pro Max packs the largest battery ever in a mainstream smartphone at just 203 grams, while leaks point to an even bigger 12,000mAh model on the horizon as silicon-carbon chemistry rewrites the battery rulebook.
body:
• Honor has launched the X80 Pro Max in China with an 11,000mAh silicon-carbon battery — the largest ever in a mainstream smartphone — at a starting price of approximately $250.
  • Despite the massive battery, the phone weighs just 203 grams and measures 8.08mm thick, lighter than both the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and Google Pixel 10 Pro XL.
  • Honor is reportedly testing a 12,000mAh battery phone, likely the Power 3 with a MediaTek Dimensity 8600 chipset, which would set yet another record.
  • The company plans to expand its 10,000mAh-plus lineup to seven devices total, far ahead of competitors Oppo, Xiaomi, and Huawei.

Honor has officially launched the X80 Pro Max in China, and its headline specification rewrites what budget smartphones can deliver: an 11,000mAh battery that the company claims will last up to 33.5 hours of short video playback or 23.9 hours of continuous gaming. The starting price of CNY 1,699 (approximately $250) makes it one of the most aggressive value propositions in the smartphone market.

The phone ships with 90W SuperCharge wired fast charging and 27W reverse wired charging, effectively turning it into a portable power bank for other devices. Honor claims the silicon-carbon battery can retain at least 80% of its health after six years of use.

Silicon-Carbon: The Technology Behind the Numbers

The battery breakthrough is driven by silicon-carbon anode technology, which allows manufacturers to dramatically increase capacity without proportionally increasing device size. Traditional lithium-ion cells hit a density ceiling that forced companies to choose between battery life and portability. Silicon anodes have a theoretical capacity more than ten times higher than conventional graphite, enabling the jump from the 5,000mAh standard to five-figure territory.

Honor uses a CVD (chemical vapor deposition) process to embed silicon atoms into a carbon framework, achieving a reported silicon content of 25% and an energy density of 901Wh/L. The result is a phone that weighs just 203 grams at 8.08mm thick — lighter than Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra (214g) and Google's Pixel 10 Pro XL (232g), despite carrying roughly double the battery capacity.

The Specs Behind the Battery

Beyond the battery, the X80 Pro Max runs on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 5 chipset paired with up to 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. The 6.8-inch AMOLED display features a 120Hz refresh rate and a claimed peak brightness of 10,000 nits — though that figure applies only to a small HDR highlight area during video playback. The phone runs Android 16 with MagicOS 10 and carries IP68/IP69K dust and water resistance ratings.

The camera setup is straightforward for a budget device: a 50MP main sensor with optical image stabilization and an 8MP selfie camera. An under-display optical fingerprint scanner, NFC, an IR blaster, and Bluetooth 6.0 round out the feature set. The phone is available in Mystic Black, Lightning Red, Moonlight White, and Vibrant Orange.

12,000mAh on the Horizon

Honor is not stopping at 11,000mAh. According to leaks from well-known tipster Digital Chat Station, the company is developing the Honor Power 3 with a battery capacity between 11,000 and 12,000mAh, powered by MediaTek's upcoming Dimensity 8600 chipset built on a 3nm process. A move to a more efficient manufacturing node could extend battery life even further.

The Power 3 would succeed the Honor Power 2, which launched in January 2026 with a 10,080mAh battery. If Honor keeps its release cadence, the Power 3 could appear in early 2027, alongside additional gaming-oriented Win 2 models. The company is also reportedly testing a dual-cell 10,000mAh battery design that could enable 120W fast charging on ultra-large batteries without overheating.

A Segment Honor Intends to Own

Honor currently manufactures three of the four 10,000mAh-class phones available in China, with the Vivo Y600 Pro as the only competitor. With plans to expand to seven devices in this category, Honor is positioning battery endurance as its core brand identity.

Other Chinese manufacturers are approaching the space more cautiously. Oppo, Xiaomi, and Huawei are all rumored to be developing similar devices, but each is expected to launch a single model before committing further. Honor's strategy of flooding the segment may force the industry to follow or risk ceding the battery-conscious consumer entirely.
